name: Node.js

levelNotes.1: Use one runtime API in a simple way (fs/promises, path, Buffer, events).
levelNotes.5: Good depth topics: stream backpressure, pipeline() error propagation, EventEmitter error semantics, AbortSignal plumbing.
levelNotes.7: Good depth topics: custom Transform streams, worker_threads pools, graceful shutdown, async_hooks-free context passing.

image.dockerfile:
FROM node:24-slim
WORKDIR /opt/eco
RUN npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install --no-audit --no-fund typescript@5.8.3 vitest@2.1.9 fastify@5.2.1 zod@3.23.8 && npm cache clean --force && ln -s /opt/eco/node_modules/.bin/tsc /usr/local/bin/tsc

ecosystem.conventions: Tests use vitest 2.1 (describe/it/expect, it.each, vi.fn, vi.spyOn, vi.useFakeTimers) in tests/*.test.{mjs,ts}; they load the code under test from ../$TARGET/ with a dynamic import, written EXACTLY like this because Vite only resolves template-string imports one level deep (bugs/<name>/ is two): `const target = new URL(`../${process.env.TARGET ?? "starter"}/solution.mjs`, import.meta.url).href; const { fn } = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ target);` (use solution.ts for TypeScript). Libraries resolve from the test run's node_modules (already set up by the test command): import them normally. fastify 5.2 and zod 3.23 are available. HTTP handlers are tested IN MEMORY with fastify's app.inject() (never listen on a port; the sandbox has no network). Use fastify schemas or zod for request validation, hooks for cross-cutting concerns, and proper status codes and error payloads.

areas.name: HTTP handlers with fastify (routes, status codes, inject tests)
Hooks/middleware: auth, rate limits, request ids
Pagination, filtering and idempotency in APIs
